title: WWDC 2000
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
Thank you.

Thank you very much for coming this morning.

We've got a lot of stuff to tell you. Uh, in addition to everybody here and the overflow rooms, uh, I'd like to also mention that we're webcasting this, uh, with ourselves, with QuickTime Live, uh, and using our partner Akamai. We now have over 14,000 live streams and climbing. We're broadcasting these streams up to a gigabit per second. So we're broadcasting now 4 gigabits per second live, uh, out of the Akamai network, uh, using QuickTime. So we've got people all over the country watching this as well.

So let's get started.

I'd first like to start with something that every, almost every Mac user touches.

And that's the mouse.

This, as you may know, is our mouse. And, uh, some people don't like it.

And we, we have many faults, but we do listen. And, uh, so, you know, some people think that this is the worst mouse in the world. We'd like to change that. And today, we are introducing a new mouse.

Now, this mouse, we may go from what some people think is the worst mouse in the industry to the best.

The first thing about this mouse that's extraordinary is it's optical. It uses optical tracking technology.

And there are some tremendous benefits with this. It is the highest precision optical mouse on the market. There are no moving parts. There's no mouse balls to ever clean. There's no performance degradation over time. And you get this optical precision without a mouse pad on almost any surface. So you can farewell mouse pad.

We're really, really happy with this. Now, you may ask, you know, this is really beautiful and there's this continuous surface over the whole thing, where's the button? Oh my God, Apple's gone from a one-button mouse to a no-button mouse.

No, not quite. Because it turns out that this whole continuous surface is the button. The entire surface is the button. It just levers down in the front. It fits any hand, whether it's a child's small hand or an adult's large hand, whether you're right-handed or left-handed. It works with any style. Some people like to click the mouse with just one finger. Some people plop their whole palm on it. It works with any style. And it's got adjustable force, whether you like a delicate button or a slightly heavier push. The entire surface is this beautiful ergonomic button and it works really, really well.

So the new Apple Mouse. Now, this turned out so well. We've been developing this for a while. It turned out so well that we want every Mac owner who uses a mouse to have it. And so we are going to make this new Apple optical mouse standard across our entire desktop line.

It is the first time anyone has ever made an optical mouse standard with a personal computer. And we're going to do it across our entire desktop line. Now, to go with such a great new mouse, we've also designed a new keyboard.

And again, this keyboard responds to some of the requests we've got, because the most popular keyboard in Apple's history was the Apple Extended Keyboard, and we've gone with that layout. We have separate cursor clusters, full-size function keys. We even have volume keys, and there's a key right on the keyboard to eject your disc. So it's really, really nice. And again, we are going to make this standard across our entire desktop line.

Now, if you own a Mac, and you say, "My God, I'd, I'd sure like one of these or both of these," we're going to be selling them as upgrades for only $59 each, and you will be able to buy them on the Apple Store only. We're taking orders today and we'll be delivering them in September. So go ahead and get in the queue, and I think you'll really, really like this.

So, we're going to go from what some people feel is, uh, a, uh, maybe the worst mouse in the industry to what we feel is the best mouse in the industry. And we thought it was so cool that we want to let everyone know, and so we're going to make a TV commercial, and I'd love to show it to you now. Let's go ahead and roll it.

Isn't that great?

All right. So, brand new optical mouse, new pro keyboard, standard on every desktop computer. Now let's get into the computers that they're going to come standard on.

This is our product matrix as you know. So let's start with the Power Mac G4.

Power Mac G4 is an awesome product. Our pro customers love this product. They can get at every component in a few seconds. And of course, it's based on the awesome power of the PowerPC G4 chip. This chip's incredible, and it has something inside it that makes it run even faster called the Velocity Engine. Now the Velocity Engine allows this chip to run at over three and a half gigaflops per second. A gigaflop is a billion instructions per second. How, how fast is that? I mean, it's hard to conceive of what is a gigaflop. Well, let me give you an example. Light travels at about 300 million meters a second, or about 186,000 miles a second. In a billionth of a second, light travels about a foot, right?

When this thing's executing three and a half billion instructions per second, in the time it takes to execute one of those instructions, light travels about 4 inches.

An amusing side note to this is, when you're executing instructions this fast, in the time it takes to execute one instruction, the light which has left your display hasn't even reached your face. That's how fast this is. And we're shipping these chips running at 500 MHz today.

Now you might ask, how does a 500 MHz G4 compare to a 1000 MHz Pentium 3, or what's more commonly known as a gigahertz? How does a 500 MHz G4 stack up against a gigahertz Pentium 3? Well, we'd like to show you right now. And so I'd like to invite Phil Schiller on stage, our Vice President of Worldwide Product Marketing.

We have, we have the best customers in the world. Many of you are here today. And some of our customers do all sorts of graphic things, graphic arts, uh, and one of them is make movie posters. So we can get some great data from some folks that we, uh, work with in Hollywood on some of these great movie posters and it makes for great comparisons in Photoshop. So tell us what we've got here today, Phil.

All right, let's do our shootout. Count us down, Phil.

All right.

Pentium's thinking.

This is the kind of stuff that a lot of our customers do many, many, many times a day. And if they can save a few seconds on each iteration, it amounts to an hour or two a day.

Great. So, what does this tell us? What does this tell us? We have a 500 MHz G4 against a gigahertz Pentium. If you measure the time on these, the Pentium got done in 124 seconds. The G4 completed this task in 100 seconds. And we have dozens of cases like this we could show you if we had enough time this morning. So what does this mean? If you do the math, it means a 500 MHz G4 is as fast as a 1.2 GHz Pentium would be if you could buy one.

Okay? That's what the tests show. And it's pretty amazing. So, we've got ourselves a really, really fast chip here, and it illustrates that it's not just megahertz, it's architecture of the chip and the system that contributes to performance. Megahertz is important, but it's not the only factor as we've just seen here. But you know, we got to thinking, having one really fast processor is great. But you know, two brains are better than one.

What if we could harness the power of two G4 chips at the same time? Well, that's exactly what we're going to do. We have a dual processor G4 here. And I'd like to invite Phil back up to find out how a dual processor G4 runs against a gigahertz Pentium running the same test. Let's roll.

All right.

Now, we could wait for the gigahertz Pentium or not. Uh, why don't we move on?

So, 500 MHz dual processor G4 on that side, gigahertz Pentium 3, and the times, the same 124 seconds by the time the Pentium completes, 61 seconds on the dual processor Power Mac G4.

If you do the math, that is equivalent to a 2 GHz Pentium 3, if you could buy one. You may be able to buy one in 12 to 18 months. We're going to deliver dual processor G4 machines starting today.

We're also running at over 7 gigaflops, 7 billion instructions per second in these machines. So, what are we going to do with this technology? We have three models of Power Mac G4s, all at really attractive prices, 400 MHz, 450 and 500 MHz. Here's what we're going to do. The 400 MHz model will continue to have a single 400 MHz processor in it. The 450 MHz model, however, is going to come standard with two 450 MHz G4s, and the high-end model is going to come standard with two 500 MHz G4 chips. You will not even be able to buy the two high-end models with a single processor. They're going to come standard with dual processors. It is going to be the first personal computers in history to come standard with dual processors.

But we're not done yet. We've got more. On each of these models, on every Power Mac model, we are also adding gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard.

Gigabit Ethernet is the new next generation of Ethernet technology that runs at a gigabit instead of 100 megabits that most systems run at now. This is very expensive stuff if you go add a card into your computer. We are building it onto the motherboard so it doesn't even take a slot. This stuff is really fast and opens up some whole new application areas for our pro customers. So to show us a little bit of that, here's Phil Schiller again.

between the server and the desktop.

Now, my boss has just disconnected the network on me to prove it.
We're on Ethernet.

Pretty cool.

So,

Gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard on all three Power Mac models.
And we're upping the storage as well.
20 gigabytes, 30 gigabytes, and 40 gigabytes built into these products, taking only one of the three drive bays.
So you can expand with two additional drives inside if you want beyond even this.
And of course, our new optical mouse and pro keyboard.
So we're doing all of this.
Dual processor standard on the top two models.
Gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard.
More storage in every model and our new optical mouse and keyboard, and we're doing it all for the same price.

Our teams have worked so hard to be able to throw this stuff in basically without changing prices at all.
We're very happy and all of these models are available today.

So, we have got a really fast chip and a really fast system architecture.
But because two brains are better than one, we're going to make multiprocessing with dual processor standard in the top two Power Mac models, and we think that this is going to be the best Power Mac ever, not only the fastest Macintosh, but continue the Power Max tradition as being the fastest personal computer in the world.

So, now the next thing I'd like to talk about is Mac OS 10.

Mac OS 10 is our new operating system as you may know.
It's rewritten from the ground up.
It's got preemptive multitasking, it's got protected memory, it's got much more modern networking, great plumbing.
It's also got a great new user interface called Aqua, and it also supports what's called symmetric multiprocessing to take full advantage of those dual processors in the new Power Max.
So when you buy one of those new Power Max with dual processors, you're ready for OS 10.
We're on track to ship a public beta of Mac OS 10 in September, I think the very early part of September, and we are on track to release Mac OS 10 very early in 2001, and it's looking great.
And we don't have time to give a full-blown demo today, but I'd like to give you just a demo of the of the user interface in case you've never seen it before.
So let me do that now.

This is Mac OS 10.
And uh a few things very quickly.
I'll just uh launch a document here.
And real quick, as you notice when I move windows around the screen, the whole window moves, not just the outline.
That's also true when I resize things, right?
Really nice.
And um one of the problems we wanted to solve was when you get these dialogues up and you don't know which application or window they're attached to, especially in a true multitasking system.
You may want to go do something else for a while and come back and you have no idea what window that dialogue went with.
Plus you have to manage that dialogue window separately.
So here's what we've done to solve that.
If this is a window, we can say, boom, that's my save panel.
Right on the window.
And so there can be no question which window this is associated with.
And when you're done, boom, it just goes away.
That's simple.
And you may ask, well, what happens if the window is really small?
Well, if the window is really small, it just does this.

And what happens if the window is off screen?
Well, it just does this.
Right?
So everything's been taken care of and now we don't have to manage our dialogues like they are more windows.
I want to show you one other thing about the save panel.
This illustrates some of the philosophy of Mac OS 10.
You've probably never seen a save panel this simple on any computer before.
When you want to save something, you name it and you simply push it this pop-up list that says where.
And in here, it's listed my the desktop, my favorite places, and the recent places I've been.
And I can pick any one of those and save.
Very simple.
But if I want to save somewhere else, I just pop this little control down here and I get a very sophisticated browser here that'll let me go anywhere.
So let's say I want to go into Avi's home directory and save this in Avi's public folder.
I can even add Avi's public folder to my favorites so that the next time, boom, I get this right in here.
I've got Avi's public folder.
So you have complexity when you need it, but we hide it when you don't need it so that the user interface can be much, much simpler.
Next, I'd like to just show you the finder.
The finder is really simple.
There's been some misconceptions about it too.
If you like your hard disk on the desktop, just drag it out.
And uh very easy to just launch a finder by clicking it just like you're used to right now.
We also let you uh show and hide the toolbar.
And uh so I'm going to use it today.
I'll keep it out.
And here's your computer and you can just navigate down here just like you've uh you've done before.
And I can navigate down to my documents as an example.
And as you can see, I don't have to have gritting turned on.
I can put them anywhere I want to, make any kind of a mess that I like.
And but we save you this work because to navigate down to the most popular places because we populate this top with some shortcuts.
So I can get to docs just by clicking this button or apps or my favorites or my home or other users or the computer.
And it's very, very easy uh to move around.
Now, I also have different views on things.
I have icon view, I have list view, and I have a new browser view.
And I can click back and forth between them with this little control on every finder window.
So we know what icon and list view are, but you may not have seen browser view before.
Browser view is very simple.
It lets me start anywhere and just browse along these columns.
So I'll pick in my home directory, pick my documents, and uh I can pick one.
I even have a preview mode.
And I can see exactly where I've been.
I can click anywhere back there to go back and I've got a little previewer here for things.
I can even preview uh movies if I want to, you know.

[Music]

I can uh even have QuickTime VR previews, you know, if I want.
And uh I can even preview MP3s if I want to, you know.

[Music]

You get the idea.
Now, the next thing I'd like to show you is the dock.

The dock is wonderful.
It's a place to put those apps you use the most, those documents you use the most, and miniaturize windows.
So this is the dock and anyone can change the size of the dock to anything that suits them.
They can have it small, they can have it big.
And when you put more things in the dock, it just shrinks to fit.
So let me go back as an example to add an application.
I can add an application like an image capture app anywhere in here.
Just drop it down and boom, the dock shrinks.
And I can move things around in the dock, change any order that I might like.
I can also add a bunch of apps at one time if I choose to.
I can add all these apps and again, you can see the dock shrink a little bit more.
These are just links.
So when I'm done using this app, I can just drag these out and it just breaks the link, very simple.

No problema.
Uh I can also add documents in the dock and it solves an age-old problem on the Macintosh, which is miniaturization.
When you're working on something and you want to go work on something else for a little while and get it out of the way, right now our miniaturization, this window shade thing, doesn't really get it out of the way.
It leaves this big window shade on your desk.
So what we've built in is the following.
You just miniaturize a window and boom, it's right there with its thumbnail automatically built for you.
Let me show you this in slow motion.
It's kind of fun to watch.
Just the craftsmanship that the team has built into this is amazing.
Isn't that nice?

Watch this.
Even if it's down here, watch what it does.

Isn't that nice?
So you always know where something's coming from and where it's going to, and you have these at your disposal uh right in the dock and just click on them and boom, they're back where you left them.
Now, I'd like to show you one last thing.
Uh let me bring up a QuickTime file, the Mission Impossible trailer.
And uh we can go ahead and uh play it here.

[Movie Trailer]

Agent.
Okay.
So uh let me show you something.
Look at this.
I put it in slow-mo here.
Isn't that cool?

[Movie Trailer]

So uh one last thing.
I'll show you uh one of the wonderful benefits of Mac OS 10.
We've got this app we wrote called the bomb app and the bomb app does everything it can to crash the system.
It rewrites low memory, it does all the nasty things that programmers are never supposed to do.
I apologize in advance for this application.

[Movie Trailer]

And this app did pretty cool.

So a brief overview of Mac OS 10.
All righty.
Now, we've been working with a lot of our developer partners very closely, but none more closely than Adobe.
Adobe's right down the block from us.
We have a fantastic relationship with them and I'd like to invite Bruce Chizen, the president of Adobe up on stage to say a few words.
Bruce.

Thanks Steve.
How you doing?
So it's clear from the Photoshop demo that we do work really closely with Apple.
We have hundreds of engineers that are working with them on getting our applications over to OS 10.
They are extremely impressed and we are absolutely committed to putting those apps, all of those key apps.
Um so as Apple rolls out OS 10, Adobe will be there.
Many of you are Adobe customers and you're using applications like InDesign, Go Live, Premiere, After Effects, and of course Photoshop to create compelling websites, print publications, videos.
The challenge is you're working with extremely large files, large and complex files.
And you need those files to be manipulated quickly.
Well, you need a quick system.
And now we have the ultimate system to create those compelling websites and that is the new G4 MP.
It is truly the ultimate Photoshop machine.
So Steve, thanks.
I can't wait to get my hands on one.

Thank you, Bruce.
Get him one.
Okay, so that's Mac OS 10.
Now, next, I'd like to talk about another partner that we work very closely with, and that's Microsoft.
Our relationship with Microsoft has been getting better and better.
We've been working with them very closely on another major new product for Mac customers, and that is the new version of Office for Macintosh, Microsoft Office 2001.
It looks terrific and to show it to us, I'd like to uh bring up Kevin Brown, the general manager of the Macintosh business unit at Microsoft.

Five or 10 minutes on homepage builder and add that quick time movie to your personal website which is hosted by Apple 24x7 at no charge and anyone can access it.
Pretty amazing.

Today, we've talked about a lot of things.
New Power Mac G4s with dual processors as standard in the top two models, as fast as a theoretical 2 gigahertz Pentium.
We've talked about new iMacs in stunning new colors, aggressive new price points, amazing new features.
We've talked about Mac OS 10 coming soon, Microsoft Office 2001 coming soon, all the Bungie games continuing to come to the Mac, iMovie 2 and homepage builder.
That's a lot for one day.
But there's one more thing.

This is our product strategy that we announced about two and a half years ago, the four quadrants.
And it's served us very well.
We've filled them all in and we've even had a chance to go around and update most of them two or three times each to constantly keep them fresh and aggressive.
But today, the first time in two and a half years, we are expanding our product strategy.
And it's not a portable.
It is a new desktop machine.
What is it?

We are combining the power of the Power Mac G4, the awesome power of this machine with the desktop elegance, the silence and the miniaturization that we learned from doing the iMacs to make a whole new class of machine.
And so, we're starting with the G4 power, we're building in a really fast G4 chip into this new machine.
We're building in the ability to have up to a gigabyte and a half of memory in the machine.
We're building in the ability to have up to 40 gigabytes of storage inside the machine.
We're adding IO for everything, modem, 100 megabit per second Ethernet, USB and firewire.
You can hook up to almost anything with this machine.
And airport wireless networking inside as well.
Now, I know some of you are saying, well, looks like a mid-range Power Mac G4 to me.
What's so new and special about this?
Well, this is where we get into the iMac magic.
Because if this is the size of a Power Mac G4, we have miniaturized all that power into something this size.
Okay?
From this to this.
And what we've miniaturized it into is an 8 inch cube.
An 8 inch cube.
Unbelievable.
Another way of looking at this is, if this is the Power Mac G4 and you could break it into four equal parts, we have miniaturized all the power into just one of those parts, which is an 8 inch cube.
Unbelievable.
Now, you can imagine with all this power in such a dense space, we must need a turbo fan to cool this thing.
But no.
Our engineers have done some brilliant work and all this power in an 8 inch cube has cooled without a fan.
And so, it runs in virtual silence in an 8 inch cube.
And we call this new product the Power Mac G4 Cube or more affectionately the G4 Cube.
And I would like to show it to you now.
Let's bring it out.

This is a stunning product, quite possibly the most beautiful product we've ever designed.
The computer is in an 8 inch cube and it's suspended in a stunning crystal clear enclosure.
There's also a slot load DVD drive, but where is it you ask?

That cool?
Wish you didn't see it?
So everything is in there, very conveniently located to sit right next to you on your desk.
Now, our engineers spent an enormous amount of energy figuring out how to get this amazingly powerful G4 technology into this 8 inch cube and to cool it without a fan.
But they also spent enormous amount of time figuring out how to get it out quickly.
Because our pro customers like to get at every component in a system within a matter of a few seconds.
So here's what we did.
You can take your Power Mac G4 and simply turn it over.
Right?
Let's get the video here.
I want you to see this.
You push down on this handle and it pops up and you literally lift all of the technology out.

You have access.
You have access to every single component.
And when you're done, you just put it back in, pop down the handle to lock it in.
We even have a Kensington lock to make sure you're the only one that opens your G4 cube.
Pop it right back over and you're in business.
Pretty nice.

So, the G4 Cube.
It's amazing.
DVD drive in the top.
Amazing cooling system through a center channel that cools the whole thing with air so that it runs in virtual silence.
The G4 Cube.
And again, a size comparison with the Power Mac shows how small it really is.
And just like the Power Mac allows you to access any component in seconds, so does the G4 Cube allow you to get at every component in just seconds.
We're very, very proud of this.
But we didn't stop there.
We designed a whole system.
And so we've worked with Harman Kardon to design a pair of Apple design stereo speakers that are gorgeous.
And obviously our new optical mouse and pro keyboard comes with the system as well.
And the system is really beautiful.
And for a system like this that's configured with a 450 MHz G4, 64 meg memory, 20 gigabytes of storage, slot load DVD drive, firewire and iMovie, for this whole system, $17.99.

And we have a second model that features a 500 MHz G4 processor, 128 megabytes of memory, 30 gigs of hard storage, DVD ROM, firewire, iMovie, make the ultimate iMovie machine.
And it's available for $22.99 and this is an Apple online store exclusive.
So you can just go to the Apple online store and order this.
All models are available in early August, just a few weeks away.
Power Mac G4 Cube.
We are so proud of this thing.
It is a complete system in every way.
Except for displays.
Oh yeah.
We have three new displays we're introducing today.
We'd like to bring them out now.
They are in equally stunning designs.

The first, a new CRT display.
It's a 17-inch Diamondtron display that's naturally flat on the front.
It's totally flat and as you can see, you can see all the way through it in the back.
It's really stunning.
And it's got this good stand on it as well that's very beautiful.
It's got two USB ports built into the display.
So you can plug your keyboard into the display.
You don't have to have cables going back to the computer.
It's got color sync built in.
We calibrated it at the factory, it stays calibrated through the life of the display.
And maybe the coolest thing.
You know how you have a lot of cable clutter on your desk with all sorts of power cables and other kinds of cables?
Well, this display is powered from the computer.
One cable carries video, USB and power from the computer.
So there's only one cable replacing three.

And $499.
Next display.
A 15-inch flat LCD.
It's really beautiful.
It's a perfect companion to the G4 Cube.
It's got 1024x768 resolution.
Again, two USB ports.
It's got touch controls on it to bring up the display controls or even to put your system to sleep and wake it up.
And it is powered from the computer with one cable just like the other.
$999.
Very aggressive.
Makes a beautiful companion to the new G4 Cube.
And our cinema display, we have a new cinema display that's enhanced to again be powered from the computer with only one cable carrying USB, video and power over the one cable.
All three of these displays go on sale today and all three of them work not only with the G4 Cube but with the Power Mac as well.
So three new displays.
We've got a video we'd like to show you about this amazing new system.
So let's roll it.

We've been working on this for a long time and it's so great to be able to tell you about it today.
The new Power Mac G4 Cube takes its place in an expanded product line.
And if you've noticed, all three of our desktop product lines which constitute over 75% of our unit volume are all new as of today.

It's amazing.
And I would like, you know, it is, it is a privilege to be able to be on the same team as the talented people at Apple.
These people are not only so talented, but they're emotional.
They're passionate and they love, they put love into these products.
And I hope you can see that today.
And I'd like all the Apple folks in the audience to stand up and all the folks on the satellite feed back in Cupertino and the other sites to stand up, please.
Let's give them a round of applause.

I don't think there's another team on the planet that could be creating products like this.
So, thank you for coming today.
We've had a lot.
And I started with the mouse.
I'd like to end with the mouse.
This optical mouse is the symbol of all the new products today for me.
It comes with all the new products that you saw and it's also just a better way of doing things, not doing things the same old way but innovating.
And it came out so wonderful that not only are we going to bundle it with all our desktop computers, but I want all of you to be the first ones to get your hands on it.
And so we're going to give you one today.

As you, as you leave the auditorium, as you leave the auditorium, if you have one of these tickets, you will be handed a new Apple optical mouse and in just a second you'll find that you can get one of these tickets under your seats.
So thank you very much for coming today.
We've enjoyed showing you all our new stuff.
